public_rationale: Under the ordinary domain-specific reading, the universal claim is too strong. The chess experiment finds learned board-state representations and changes move generation by intervening on them. That goes beyond evidence of surface imitation alone. The result does not show that deployed chatbots possess complete, reliable world models. Because Marcus leaves proper and the scope of LLMs undefined, this proposal explicitly depends on including specialized language models and allowing useful but imperfect representations.
limitations: The decisive counterexample is a domain-trained language model.
A causally used board representation does not establish general intelligence or comprehensive understanding.
The stronger requirement of flawless or fully general world modeling is not tested.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs never induce proper world models of anything; everything they do is mimicry.

statement.excerpt: It is not just that LLMs fail to induce proper world models of chess. It’s that they never induce proper worlds of anything. Everything that they do is through mimicry, rather than abstracted cognition across proper world models.
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

our_interpretation: Read the categorical wording as denying learned internal models in every domain, including bounded domains such as board games.
The ordinary testable reading of a world model is an internal representation of domain state that tracks changes and helps determine predictions or actions. It need not be flawless.
Require evidence of causal use, not merely that a probe can decode information from activations.
Include language models trained specifically on domain sequences; Marcus supplies no explicit exclusion for such models.
Never covers the history through publication, so the target has no specified lower bound.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that the relevant language models use only surface imitation and never learn and use internal domain-state representations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one language model learns a domain-state representation from sequences, tracks state across those sequences, and uses that representation causally in its predictions.

evidence.explanation: The chess-trained language model encodes board positions, and changing those internal representations changes move generation while leaving the input game text unchanged. This is a counterexample to universal absence under the stated reading, although it is a specialized model.

evidence.explanation: This study reports learned board structure across several language-model families but also finds weaknesses in generating consecutive moves. It limits any inference from internal representations to robust, general competence.
